critical_code_review_comments: OK · eod_flatten.py FLATTEN_END_MIN == QUIET_START_MIN (imported from eod_quiet, not hardcoded) — the flatten window deliberately ends exactly where the EA v1.41 quiet window begins, so queued FULL_CLOSEs are picked up by the EA before it defers order ops. Strong coupling with eod_quiet.QUIET_START_MIN prevents drift.

OK · sweep_eod_flatten trades.find filter is `{'account_id': str(_id), 'status': 'open', 'origin': 'auto'}` — manual trades are excluded at the query level, not just filtered post-fetch. Confirmed by TestSweep.test_manual_trades_never_touched which asserts the filter args include origin=='auto' and status=='open'.

OK · Idempotency guard: `if tr.get('pending_modification'): continue` — a trade already carrying a FULL_CLOSE/MODIFY_SL/etc from the prior sweep or from an explicit user-side action is left alone; the next sweep re-checks and only queues if pending clears. No double-queue possible.

OK · Broker-time correctness: `broker_now = now + timedelta(seconds=broker_offset_sec)` — the offset applied to server UTC gives broker wall-clock. Bounds 23:15-23:40 evaluated in minutes-of-broker-day. For a UTC+3 broker the flatten window at 20:15-20:40 UTC lines up exactly with the EA's own 23:15-23:40 broker clock. Unit test test_broker_offset_shifts_window explicitly covers this.

OK · server.py _eod_flatten_loop is a while-True 60s cadence with try/except around sweep_eod_flatten — the loop cannot die from a single sweep exception; registered at startup via asyncio.create_task alongside _eod_quiet_task and the other loops (L506 area).

OK · bot_runner.py L764-766 correctly chains `eod_quiet_block(...) or eod_flatten_block(...)` so BOTH vetoes are surfaced through the same pulse SKIP path (inc_intel_counter still fires 'eod_quiet_block' for both — see observation below).

OK · scalp/engine.py _maybe_evaluate uses `elif (eod_reason := _eod_flatten_block(self.account))` right after eod_quiet in the risk chain (L623), so flatten veto stops signals from being evaluated (not just submitted) — earliest possible short-circuit. Import at L41 top of module keeps it out of hot-path per-tick imports.

OK · Notification insert is best-effort (`try/except Exception: pass` at L100) — a broken notifications collection cannot stall the close-queue. Also emitted only when acct_queued > 0 (no empty spam) and once per account per sweep (loop-level not trade-level).

OK · EOD_FLATTEN_ENABLED default 'true'; false is checked lowercase — the flag correctly short-circuits BOTH eod_flatten_block (returns None so no veto) and sweep_eod_flatten (returns {'enabled': False, ...} before touching accounts.find). Verified live and via unit tests.

OBSERVATION · bot_runner.py L771 inc_intel_counter(user_id, 'eod_quiet_block') is invoked when EITHER eod_quiet_block OR eod_flatten_block returns a reason — the intel counter conflates the two windows. Non-blocking (both are 'EOD safety'), but if you want per-window telemetry you'd want a second counter 'eod_flatten_block' when the reason string begins with 'EOD flatten window'. Trivial follow-up.

OBSERVATION · The sweep uses `str(acc['_id'])` for account_id matching against trades.account_id — assumes trades store account_id as a string form of the account's ObjectId (or the account 'id' field). If any older trades in the collection store account_id as an ObjectId directly or under a different field, they would be silently skipped. Existing collection-wide invariants elsewhere in the codebase suggest string form is standardized, but worth an integration check on the first live production sweep window (a one-time log of `queued/expected` ratio would surface any mismatch).

OBSERVATION · sweep_eod_flatten is queued once every 60s from _eod_flatten_loop. Window is 25 minutes wide (23:15-23:40 broker) → up to 25 sweep iterations per account per day. First iteration queues everything, subsequent iterations no-op due to pending_modification guard — cheap. Even for 5000 open positions the second-through-25th iterations are `find(...).__aiter__ + skip on pending_modification` which is O(n) Mongo scan; consider adding a compound index on {account_id:1, status:1, origin:1, pending_modification:1} if per-account open count grows past a few hundred. Non-blocking today.

OBSERVATION · The best-effort notification catches bare Exception. If mongo is momentarily unreachable the close still gets queued (correct behavior). The trade-update update_one however is NOT wrapped in try/except — a single failed Mongo write raises out of the sweep and (thanks to server.py loop-level try/except) will just retry in the next 60s window. Acceptable.
OBSERVATION · Module size all good: eod_flatten.py is 102 lines, well under the 700-line file-size ceiling. Clean single-responsibility module.
